The type of isomerism present in nitropentammine chromium (III) chloride is
solution:
The formula is $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$. It can exist as $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$ (pentaamminenitrochromium(III) chloride) and $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{ONO})]\text{Cl}_2$ (pentaamminenitritochromium(III) chloride).

Therefore the isomerism is linkage isomerism, as the $\text{NO}_2$ group is linked through N as $-\text{NO}_2$ or through O as $-\text{ONO}$.

stem: Identify, from the following, the diamagnetic, tetrahedral complex
solution:
(a) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$; $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing: $sp^3$, tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

(b) In $[\text{Co}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$, oxalate is bidentate, giving an octahedral structure.

(c) In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand causing pairing of 3d electrons: $dsp^2$, square planar and diamagnetic.

(d) In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, Ni is in zero oxidation state ($3d^84s^2$). CO is a strong field ligand causing pairing of 3d and 4s electrons: $sp^3$, tetrahedral and diamagnetic.

Hence (D) is the correct answer.

What is X in the following reaction?

$\text{CO} + 2\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{X} \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$
solution: The given reaction is the industrial preparation of methanol from a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen. The gaseous mixture is subjected to 200 atmosphere and then passed over heated catalyst mixture of ZnO and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$ kept at $573-673$ K. Methanol vapours formed are then condensed to liquid.

stem: When the same quantity of electricity is passed through the aqueous solutions of the given electrolytes for the same amount of time, which metal will be deposited in maximum amount on the cathode?
solution:
$\dfrac{\text{Mass of metal}_1\text{ deposited}}{\text{Mass of metal}_2\text{ deposited}} = \dfrac{\text{Eq. wt. of metal}_1}{\text{Eq. wt. of metal}_2}$

The equivalent weight of silver is highest among the given options.

Which of the following is only a redox reaction but not a disproportionation reaction?
solution: The reaction $\text{P}_4 + 8\text{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{PCl}_3 + 2\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2 + 4\text{SO}_2$ involves change of oxidation state of P from 0 to +3 and that of S from +4 to +1/+4 (reduction). Thus, it is a redox reaction but not a disproportionation reaction.

stem: Le-Chatelier principle is not applicable to :-
solution: Le-Chatelier principle is not applicable to equilibria involving only solids, since changing concentration or pressure has no effect on them: $\text{Fe(s)} + \text{S(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{FeS(s)}$.

solution:
